name: Orroral Valley Circuit
reason: Parks ACT walking tracks (via leads): 19 km day loop from the Orroral tracking station site.

name: Orroral Campground
reason: Campground: accommodation, not a place to visit (run rule).

name: Honeysuckle Campground
reason: Campground (run rule); the tracking station site nearby is the draw, not the campground.

name: Ginini Flats Wetlands Ramsar Site
reason: Wikivoyage Namadgi 'See' names it: the ACT's only Ramsar wetland; one counted source.

name: Mount Ginini
reason: Re-looked: Wikivoyage Namadgi mentions only Mount Franklin skiing and the Ginini Flats wetland, not the peak; Wikipedia alone does not count.

name: Mount Coree
reason: No counted source found naming it as a place to go (Wikivoyage Namadgi omits it); Wikipedia only.

name: Hospital Hill Lookout
reason: Wikivoyage Namadgi lists the Boboyan Road lookout with interpretive signs and mountain views (opened); not a hospital.

name: Brandy Flat Hut
reason: Wikivoyage describes it only as a short stopover for cyclists on a firetrail: a minor roadside hut.

name: Gudgenby Homestead
reason: Wikivoyage Namadgi 'See' calls it one of the most visited huts: an 1845 homestead, restored and re-erected.

name: Orroral Homestead
reason: Wikivoyage Namadgi 'See': 1860s homestead, the oldest and best conserved hut in the park, with interpretive signs inside.

name: Brayshaws and Westermans Homesteads
reason: Part of the Settlers Track (Wikivoyage: mostly visited as a stopover for walkers of that track); keep the track.

name: Horse Gully Hut
reason: Wikivoyage: visited mostly by people camping at Mount Clear; a minor WWII-era hut.

name: Bendora Dam
reason: Wikivoyage Namadgi 'See' (and Wikipedia): 1961 arch dam, first of its type in Australia, with lookouts.

name: Corin Dam
reason: Wikivoyage Namadgi 'See' lists it (entry has no text); Corin Dam Road area is a recognised picnic and walking stop, but the visitor source says nothing of what to do.

name: Cotter Dam
reason: Wikivoyage Tuggeranong and Country ACT (counted per candidate; I could not locate the listing text) and Wikipedia note a dam-wall viewing platform and picnics; a short, accessible stop.

name: Bendora Arboretum
reason: Wikivoyage Namadgi 'See': 1940 experimental plantings, 52 species, 5 km grade-2 walk.

name: Cotter Reserve
reason: Parks ACT: the Cotter Recreation Area (river picnicking and swimming) that locals call the Cotter; the one name for the cluster of Cotter sites.

name: Cotter Campground
reason: Campground (run rule); Wikivoyage lists it under Sleep.

name: Cotter Avenue
reason: Part of the Cotter Recreation Area: one picnic site among several (barbecues, playground).

name: Cotter Bend
reason: Part of the Cotter Recreation Area: a small riverside picnic site.

name: Casuarina Sands
reason: Parks ACT (leads, riverside beach in Cotter Recreation Area): sandy Murrumbidgee beach for picnics, fishing and walks; a second-tier swimming and river stop.

name: Point Hut Crossing
reason: Parks ACT: shady Murrumbidgee crossing with sandy beaches, south end of the Discovery Track.

name: Uriarra Crossing
reason: Parks ACT: both banks of the Murrumbidgee, popular with birdwatchers.

name: Swamp Creek
reason: Part of Uriarra Crossing Recreation Area.

name: Angle Crossing
reason: Parks ACT lists it only as the southernmost river point; no sourced thing to see or do.

name: Murrays Corner
reason: Parks ACT page has little content; no visitor reason is stated.

name: Kambah Pool
reason: Two counted sources (Wikivoyage Tuggeranong/Country ACT, Parks ACT): swimming among big boulders in the Murrumbidgee, 10 min walk.

name: Bullen Range Nature Reserve
reason: Reserve known for the Red Rocks cliff climbing site, partly closed for falcons; the source lists it only as an agency park, no visit named.

name: Murrumbidgee River Corridor
reason: A 66 km linear reserve, a region of sites (Casuarina Sands, Kambah Pool, Point Hut), not one place; the sites are judged separately.

name: Lower Cotter Catchment Reserve
reason: Catchment reserve with limited visitor content read; nothing named to do.

name: ACT Bushfire Memorial
reason: A minor memorial (2006) in Stromlo Forest Park.

name: 2003 Canberra bushfires
reason: An event, not a place; no visitor source.

name: Jerrabomberra West Grasslands
reason: Parks ACT (nature reserve page, via leads): nature reserve with the 8 km Grassy Plains walk; a named walk in a reserve.

name: Callum Brae
reason: Private heritage precinct with limited access; its coordinates are in New Zealand (wrong place).

name: Centenary Trail
reason: Visit Canberra (Hall page) names a popular section to One Tree Hill; Parks ACT lists the 145 km Canberra Centenary Trail as a park; entire loop lies in the ACT.

name: Lower Molonglo Water Quality Control Centre
reason: A sewage treatment plant; no counted source found naming it as somewhere to go.

name: Hall
reason: Wikivoyage Canberra/Hall (read) and VisitCanberra give the village its own page with a See section, the 20-site National Trust Hall Heritage Walk and access to wineries and One Tree Hill; the run keeps Hall when a visitor source gives it its own listing. The monthly market is not the reason.

name: Local Spirit Distillery Cellar Door
reason: Distillery cellar door: one of several Hall venues, not singled out as a destination in its own right (run rule).

name: Pialligo Estate
reason: Winery/cellar door by appointment; visitcanberra lists it only among many wineries (winery rule).

name: Canberra District Wine Region
reason: A region of 140 cellar doors, not one place a visitor goes for half an hour.

name: Tharwa
reason: Wikivoyage Tuggeranong and Country ACT gives Tharwa Village its own listing: oldest ACT settlement, old bridge, gateway to Namadgi and Tidbinbilla (opened and read).

name: Tharwa Bridge
reason: Part of Tharwa: Wikivoyage mentions the old bridge only inside the Tharwa Village listing.

name: Cuppacumbalong Homestead
reason: Wikivoyage names only 'Cuppacumbalong Pottery' at Tharwa, a craft studio/shop; no source gives homestead tours.

name: Mugga-Mugga
reason: Wikivoyage lists the 1830s cottage with guided tours, but open only 10AM-2PM the first weekend of each month (opened and read).

name: Geoscience Australia Education Centre
reason: Wikivoyage: free geology displays of minerals, fossils, Mon-Fri 9-5 (opened and read); one source, a short visit.

name: Mount Ainslie
reason: Agency page names the summit (road, walk, bike) and Wikivoyage's North Canberra calls Ainslie Lookout Canberra's most important lookout, with the axis view to Parliament House (opened). Mount Ainslie Nature Reserve is the reserve of this peak.

name: Red Hill Nature Reserve
reason: parks.act.gov.au agency list (parks-act-leads.json, relied on): 3.2 km Red Track loop with Red Hill Lookout over central Canberra.

name: Black Mountain Nature Reserve
reason: parks.act.gov.au agency list (parks-act-leads.json, relied on): many walking tracks and city views, reached from the Botanic Gardens. Keep as the reserve; any tower or lookout on it is part of it.

name: Aranda Bushland Nature Reserve
reason: parks.act.gov.au agency list (parks-act-leads.json, relied on): named Frost Hollow to Forest Walk, 1-2 hours.

name: O'Connor Ridge Nature Reserve
reason: Small 57 ha suburban reserve; agency names no walk or lookout worth a trip.

name: Rob Roy Range Nature Reserve
reason: Restricted access; much is leased land closed to the public.

name: Molonglo River Reserve
reason: Agency Murrumbidgee/Molonglo page names it with walking tracks; one source, no specific sight named.

name: Namarag
reason: Part of Molonglo River Reserve; a recreation hub under restoration with nothing named to see.

name: Tharwa Sandwash
reason: parks.act.gov.au agency list (parks-act-leads.json, relied on): scenic picnic area on the Murrumbidgee in Gigerline Nature Reserve; keep this and reject Gigerline as the container.

name: Gigerline Nature Reserve
reason: Container of Tharwa Sandwash, the named visitor place; duplicate of it.

name: Blue Range Hut
reason: parks.act.gov.au agency list (parks-act-leads.json, relied on): historic hut in Lower Cotter Catchment; nothing in the lead says what there is to see or how to reach it.

name: Pierces Creek Forest
reason: Pine plantation; no named walk, lookout or sight.

name: Tuggeranong Pines
reason: parks.act.gov.au agency list (parks-act-leads.json, relied on): riding and walking forest in Canberra's south.

name: Melrose Nature Reserve
reason: Reserve near the NSW border with nothing named to see or do.

name: Black Mountain Peninsula District Park
reason: Lakeside district park; no guide singles it out beyond the agency list (urban park rule).

name: Canberra Nara Peace Park
reason: parks.act.gov.au agency list (parks-act-leads.json, relied on): Japanese garden with lantern in Lennox Gardens on the lake; part of Lennox Gardens District Park.

name: Canberra Beijing Garden
reason: parks.act.gov.au agency list (parks-act-leads.json, relied on): Chinese garden in Lennox Gardens on the lake, a distinct garden from Nara Peace Park.
